  • Method Details

    • coulombLawField

      public static Vector2 coulombLawField(Vector2 sourcePos, float charge, Vector2 testPoint)
      Calculates the vector representing the electric field strength at a given test point due to a given point charge, using Coulomb's law. If the test point and the point charge are within a certain minimum distance, the test point will be treated as being the miminum distance away from the point charge, to prevent the electric field strength from blowing up to infinity.
      Parameters:
      sourcePos - A vector representing the position of the point charge, in meters
      charge - The charge of the point charge, in coulombs
      testPoint - A vector representing the position of the test point, in meters
      Returns:
      A vector representing the electric field strength at the given test point, in N/C

    • ampereCircuitalLaw

      public static Vector3 ampereCircuitalLaw(Vector2 wirePoint, Vector2 current, Vector2 testPoint)
      Calculates the vector representing the magnetic field strength at a given test point due to an infinitely long current-carrying wire, using Ampère's circuital law. If the test point and the wire are within a certain minimum distance, the test point will be treated as being the miminum distance away from the wire, to prevent the electric field strength from blowing up to infinity. The line in space representing the wire is given by a point and a direction vector.
      Parameters:
      wirePoint - A vector representing a point that the wire passes through, in meters
      current - A vector representing the direction and magnitude of the current, in amperes
      testPoint - A vector representing the position of the test point, in meters
      Returns:
      A three-dimensional vector representing the electric field strength at the given test point, in teslas. Note that since the wire and test point are confined to be in 2D space, the magnetic field will only have a component in the z-direction.

    • closestPointOnLine

      public static Vector2 closestPointOnLine(Vector2 linePoint, Vector2 lineDirection, Vector2 testPoint)
      Calculates the point on a line given by a point and a direction vector that is closest to a test point, using vector projection.
      Parameters:
      linePoint - A vector representing a point that the line passes through
      lineDirection - The direction vector of the line
      testPoint - A vector representing the position of test point
      Returns:
      A vector representing the position of the point on the line closest to the test point
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if lineDirection is equal to the zero vector

    • electricForce

      public static Vector2 electricForce(float charge, Vector2 electricField)
      Calculates the vector representing electric force on a charged object due to an electric field. The resulting electric force is eequal to the charge of the object multiplied by the electric field strength.
      Parameters:
      charge - The charge of the object, in coulombs
      electricField - A vector representing the electric field experienced by the object, in N/C
      Returns:
      A vector representing the electric force on the object, in newtons

    • magneticForce

      public static Vector3 magneticForce(float charge, Vector2 velocity, Vector3 magneticField)
      Calculates the vector representing the magnetic force on a moving, charged object due to a magnetic field. The resulting magnetic force is equal to the charge of the object multiplied by the cross product of its velocity and the magnetic field strength.
      Parameters:
      charge - The charge of the object, in coulombs
      velocity - A vector representing the velocity of the object, in m/s
      magneticField - A vector representing the magnetic field experienced by the object, in teslas
      Returns:
      A vector representing the magnetic force on the object, in newtons

    • lorentzForce

      public static Vector3 lorentzForce(float charge, Vector2 electricField, Vector2 velocity, Vector3 magneticField)
      Calculates the vector representing the Lorentz force on a moving, charged object due to an electric and magnetic field. The Lorentz force is the combined total of the electric and magnetic force on an object.
      Parameters:
      charge - The charge of the object, in coulombs
      electricField - A vector representing the electric field experienced by the object, in N/C
      velocity - A vector representing the velocity of the object, in m/s
      magneticField - A vector representing the magnetic field experienced by the object, in teslas
      Returns:
      A vector representing the Lorentz force on the object, in newtons
